tEn: Migrating our Messages API to Rust
tZh: 将我们的 Messages API 迁移至 Rust
sEn: Migrating Anthropic's production Messages API from Python to Rust cut per-request CPU usage by about 70% and median time to first token by about 20%, with verification against live traffic—not code generation—proving to be the real bottleneck.
sZh: Anthropic 将生产环境的 Messages API 从 Python 迁移到 Rust，每请求 CPU 占用降低约 70%，首 token 中位时间缩短约 20%，而真正的瓶颈在于对线上流量的验证而非代码生成。
absEn: This article describes Anthropic's migration of its production Messages API from Python to Rust, motivated by roughly 1,800x traffic growth and the need to reduce per-request CPU usage. Claude generated a first version of the core request path in about a week, but the authors argue that verification, not generation, became the bottleneck: the Python API kept changing, Claude's replies are nondeterministic, and customer requests could not be read. Existing integration tests proved insufficient because they were coupled to the Python implementation and incomplete, and the Rust version passed about 98% of tests yet matched only about a quarter of production inputs. The authors turned the production API into an oracle, shadowing live traffic by running the model once and replaying its output to Rust, then comparing every stage before and after the model call. To protect privacy, they recorded only the shape of each difference through checkpointing and fingerprints, grouping mismatches by bug and dispatching agents to fix them. The resulting Rust API uses about 70% less CPU per request and cuts median time to first token by about 20% without taking the service offline or freezing feature development.
absZh: 本文介绍 Anthropic 将其生产环境的 Messages API 从 Python 迁移到 Rust 的过程，动因是流量增长约 1800 倍，以及降低每请求 CPU 占用的需求。Claude 在大约一周内生成了核心请求路径的第一版，但作者认为，真正的瓶颈在于验证而非生成：Python API 持续变动、Claude 的回复具有不确定性，且客户请求无法读取。现有集成测试被证明不够充分，因为它们与 Python 实现耦合且不完整；Rust 版本通过了约 98% 的测试，却只匹配了约四分之一的生产输入。作者将生产 API 变为 oracle，通过让模型运行一次并将其输出重放给 Rust 来影子线上流量，然后比较模型调用前后的每个阶段。为保护隐私，他们仅通过检查点和指纹记录每处差异的形状，按 bug 对不匹配进行分组，并派发智能体进行修复。最终的 Rust API 每请求 CPU 占用降低约 70%，首 token 中位时间缩短约 20%，且未使服务下线，也未冻结功能开发。

contrib.en: Migrated production Messages API from Python to Rust, cutting CPU per request ~70% and median time to first token ~20%.
contrib.zh: 将生产环境 Messages API 从 Python 迁移到 Rust，每请求 CPU 降低约 70%，首 token 中位时间缩短约 20%。

contrib.en: Identifies verification, not code generation, as the new bottleneck for live-system migrations with capable models.
contrib.zh: 指出在强模型参与下，实时系统迁移的新瓶颈是验证而非代码生成。

contrib.en: Turns the production API into an oracle: shadow live traffic, run the model once, replay output to Rust, compare every stage.
contrib.zh: 把生产 API 当作 oracle：影子实时流量，模型只跑一次，将输出重放给 Rust，逐阶段比对。

contrib.en: Uses checkpointing and fingerprints to record only the shape of diffs, protecting privacy while grouping bugs.
contrib.zh: 用检查点与指纹只记录差异的形状，在保护隐私的同时对 bug 分组。

contrib.en: Dispatches coordinating and worker agents across inner, outer, and memory loops to fix diffs autonomously with human review gates.
contrib.zh: 通过内层、外层与记忆循环调度协调与工作智能体自主修复差异，并设人工评审关卡。

contrib.en: Shows test pass rate (~98%) can diverge sharply from production input parity (~25%), motivating traffic-based verification.
contrib.zh: 表明测试通过率（约 98%）可能与生产输入一致率（约 25%）严重背离，需基于流量验证。

limits.en: Verifier rewards output matching, not fix quality; agents proposed shortcuts engineers rejected, requiring human gates.
limits.zh: 验证器奖励输出匹配而非修复质量；智能体提出被工程师否决的捷径，需人工把关。

limits.en: Inner loop is fast but imperfect: agents test only self-written requests with a local verifier not exactly like production.
limits.zh: 内层循环快但不完美：智能体仅测试自写请求，本地验证器与生产不完全一致。

limits.en: Parity is a moving target because the Python API keeps changing during migration, complicating correctness definition.
limits.zh: Python API 在迁移期间持续变化，使一致性成为移动目标，增加正确性定义难度。

limits.en: Privacy constraints prevent reading requests or replies, so agents see only fingerprints and must guess root causes.
limits.zh: 隐私限制使请求与回复不可读，智能体只能看到指纹并需猜测根因。

limits.en: Approach depends on shadowable production traffic and a stable oracle; may not transfer to systems lacking such traffic.
limits.zh: 方法依赖可影子的生产流量与稳定 oracle，未必适用于缺乏此类流量的系统。

paras.en: Many problems have a _generator–verifier_ gap: it’s often far easier to verify that a solution is correct than to come up with one. Sudoku is a classic example. It’s simple to check the solution (just count the numbers in each row, column, and box), but finding that solution can take a long time. Many ambitious Claude projects have relied on this gap: formalizing proofs in mathematics or migrating large, well-tested codebases are tasks Claude can take on as long as it has a reliable way to verify its work.
paras.zh: 许多问题存在**生成器–验证器**差距：验证一个解决方案是否正确通常比想出一个解决方案要容易得多。数独就是一个经典例子。检查解决方案很简单（只需数每行、每列和每个宫中的数字），但找到那个解决方案可能需要很长时间。许多雄心勃勃的 Claude 项目都依赖于这种差距：形式化数学证明或迁移大型、经过充分测试的代码库是 Claude 可以承担的任务，只要它有可靠的方法来验证其工作。

paras.en: But as Claude has become more capable, it’s begun to take on projects in live systems, where generating the work is easier than verifying it. In these systems, users often rely on edge cases and quirks that fall outside the test suite, and it’s hard to write a definition of “correct” that covers everything. Without a reliable way to check Claude’s work, the migration of a live system is hard to trust—however quickly Claude can generate the code for it.
paras.zh: 但随着 Claude 变得更强大，它开始承担实时系统中的项目，在这些系统中，生成工作比验证工作更容易。在这些系统中，用户经常依赖测试套件之外的边缘情况和特殊行为，而且很难写出一个涵盖所有情况的“正确”定义。没有可靠的方法来检查 Claude 的工作，实时系统的迁移就很难让人信任——无论 Claude 能多快地生成代码。

paras.en: We ran into this problem when we migrated our Messages API from Python to Rust. This API is the primary way that customers—as well as our own apps, like Claude Code and Cowork—reach Claude. From early 2024 to fall 2026, API traffic grew roughly 1,800 times. Rust would allow us to use far less CPU per request. Claude wrote a first version of the API’s core request path in about a week. But building trust in the migration required us to find a way to verify that our Rust API was at parity with our production API. This proved hard for several reasons, including that the Python API continued changing throughout the migration, so parity was a moving target; Claude can reply nondeterministically to the same request, so a difference between two outputs didn’t necessarily mean a bug; and we couldn't read customer requests, so we weren't able to easily see where the two versions diverged.
paras.zh: 当我们将 Messages API 从 Python 迁移到 Rust 时，我们遇到了这个问题。这个 API 是客户以及我们自己的应用（如 Claude Code 和 Cowork）访问 Claude 的主要方式。从 2024 年初到 2026 年秋季，API 流量增长了大约 1,800 倍。Rust 将允许我们每个请求使用更少的 CPU。Claude 在大约一周内编写了 API 核心请求路径的第一个版本。但建立对迁移的信任需要我们找到一种方法来验证我们的 Rust API 与生产 API 是否一致。这被证明很难，原因有几个，包括 Python API 在整个迁移过程中持续变化，因此一致性是一个移动的目标；Claude 对同一请求可能以非确定性的方式回复，因此两个输出之间的差异不一定意味着有 bug；而且我们无法读取客户请求，因此我们无法轻易看到两个版本在哪里出现分歧。

paras.en: In this post, we share how we turned the production Messages API itself into a verifier—and how that helped us test the new Rust version on production traffic, find where it differed, and automatically dispatch agents to fix those differences. This allowed us to ship an API on Rust that uses about 70% less CPU per request and cuts median time to first token by about 20% without ever taking the service offline or freezing feature development.
paras.zh: 在这篇文章中，我们分享了如何将生产 Messages API 本身变成一个验证器——以及这如何帮助我们在生产流量上测试新的 Rust 版本，找到它们的不同之处，并自动派遣智能体来修复这些差异。这使我们能够发布一个基于 Rust 的 API，每个请求使用的 CPU 减少约 70%，并将首次令牌的中位时间缩短约 20%，而无需让服务下线或冻结功能开发。

items.en: We built the Messages API in 2023 and wrote it in Python, which was widely used internally for much of our research code. At first, it was simple. The Messages API passed requests to the model and sent back what the model wrote. (One engineer at the time called it “basically a request forwarder.”) But as the Messages API became more capable and deeply integrated with our codebases, it also developed shared dependencies with Python libraries that were owned by our research and inference teams, which made it hard to move. If we ever wanted to move to another language, it would mean building logging, metrics, and tools all over again.
items.zh: 我们在 2023 年构建了 Messages API，并用 Python 编写，Python 在我们的研究代码中被广泛使用。起初，它很简单。Messages API 将请求传递给模型，并返回模型写出的内容。（当时一位工程师称它“基本上就是一个请求转发器”。）但随着 Messages API 变得更强大，并与我们的代码库深度集成，它也与我们的研究和推理团队拥有的 Python 库形成了共享依赖，这使得迁移变得困难。如果我们想迁移到另一种语言，就意味着要重新构建日志、指标和工具。

items.en: This calculus gradually began to change. By late 2025, every Messages API request had to be validated, converted into the prompt, tokenized, and screened by our safety classifiers. As each reply arrived, the stream of tokens had to be sorted into text, thinking, and tool calls, and Python added overhead to every one of those steps each time it created an object, freed memory, or handed its work to the next task. Traffic eventually grew far beyond what the initial Python service was built for (Figure 1), and we quickly needed to find a way to make the service much more efficient.
items.zh: 这种考量逐渐开始改变。到 2025 年底，每个 Messages API 请求都必须经过验证、转换为提示词、分词，并由我们的安全分类器筛查。当每个回复到达时，令牌流必须被分类为文本、思考和工具调用，而 Python 在每次创建对象、释放内存或将工作交给下一个任务时，都会给这些步骤增加开销。流量最终增长到远超最初 Python 服务的构建能力（图 1），我们很快需要找到一种方法使服务更加高效。

items.capEn: The monthly average of API requests per day on our own platform, including our own use.
items.capZh: 我们自有平台每日 API 请求的月平均值，包括我们自己的使用。

items.en: Full rewrites of large production systems are often approached cautiously, for at least two reasons. First, there is no guarantee that test suites cover 100% of production code behavior, and rewriting it is risky. Second, the sheer effort required often makes such work intractable. (In 2024, after one of our engineers suggested migrating to Go or Rust, another temporarily settled the question: “_We are not rewriting the API in go or rust!_”)
items.zh: 对大型生产系统进行全量重写通常需要谨慎对待，至少有两个原因。首先，无法保证测试套件覆盖生产代码行为的 100%，重写存在风险。其次，所需的大量工作往往使此类任务难以完成。（2024 年，在我们的一位工程师建议迁移到 Go 或 Rust 后，另一位工程师暂时解决了这个问题：“_我们不会用 go 或 rust 重写 API！_”）

items.en: The standard advice if you’re looking for performance gains is thus to rewrite only the parts that are slowing the system down, so that’s where we started. In Rust, we rewrote the code that parses a model’s output and called it from Python. This reduced the API’s CPU usage by about 8% to 10%. However, incremental solutions often incur added complexity, and it’s important to make sure that incremental improvements justify those costs. In our case, the gains didn’t justify the added complexity. Each token now crossed between Python and Rust three times (Figure 2), creating new sources of overhead.
items.zh: 因此，如果追求性能提升，标准建议是只重写拖慢系统的部分，我们也是从这里开始的。在 Rust 中，我们重写了解析模型输出的代码，并从 Python 中调用它。这使 API 的 CPU 使用率降低了约 8%到 10%。然而，增量解决方案往往会增加复杂性，因此必须确保增量改进值得这些成本。在我们的案例中，收益并不能证明增加的复杂性是合理的。现在每个 token 在 Python 和 Rust 之间穿越三次（图 2），产生了新的开销来源。

items.capEn: After the incremental rewrite, each token of a reply crossed between Python and Rust three times.
items.capZh: 增量重写后，回复的每个 token 在 Python 和 Rust 之间往返了三次。

items.en: As Claude became increasingly capable, we began to question whether the usual reasons to avoid a full migration still held. The effort required to undertake the project was dropping fast: by May 2026, Claude was writing more than 80% of the code Anthropic merged. We wondered if Claude could now help us write code that would empirically capture every behavior and fix in the production system. But the question became: how could we verify that the behavior of our migration was correct? Verification, not generation, had become the bottleneck.
items.zh: 随着 Claude 能力越来越强，我们开始质疑避免全量迁移的常见理由是否仍然成立。开展该项目所需的工作量正在快速下降：到 2026 年 5 月，Claude 编写的代码已占 Anthropic 合并代码的 80%以上。我们想知道 Claude 现在是否能帮助我们编写代码，以实证方式捕获生产系统中的每一个行为和修复。但问题变成了：我们如何验证迁移的行为是正确的？验证，而非生成，已成为瓶颈。

items.en: To verify the migration, we first needed to define what "correct" meant. You can do this in a few ways (Figure 3). If you're lucky, you can simply write a rule. A theorem in mathematics is a precise statement, and a proof assistant (like Lean) can check each step of a proof against a fixed set of rules. Other times—and more frequently in software engineering—you define "correct" with a set of examples, like tests. For instance, when Bun moved from Zig to Rust, its test suite was written in TypeScript, so the same tests could judge both versions. In our case, neither approach was sufficient, so we used the existing system as an oracle to test parity during the migration. In this case, our existing system (the Messages API) kept changing. We were releasing new models and shipping new features regularly, which made the definition of "correct" a moving target.
items.zh: 为了验证迁移，我们首先需要定义“正确”的含义。这可以通过几种方式实现（图 3）。如果足够幸运，你可以直接写出一条规则。数学中的定理是一个精确的陈述，而证明助手（如 Lean）可以依据一组固定规则检查证明的每一步。在其他情况下——在软件工程中更为常见——你通过一组示例（如测试）来定义“正确”。例如，当 Bun 从 Zig 迁移到 Rust 时，其测试套件是用 TypeScript 编写的，因此同一套测试可以评判两个版本。在我们的案例中，这两种方法都不够充分，因此我们在迁移期间将现有系统作为 oracle 来测试一致性。在这种情况下，我们的现有系统（Messages API）一直在变化。我们定期发布新模型并交付新功能，这使得“正确”的定义成为一个不断移动的目标。

items.en: Tests were the easiest place for us to start, since we already had an existing set of about 700 integration tests. However, two problems limited our ability to trust them to verify the correctness of a migration as high stakes as this (Figure 4).
items.zh: 测试是我们最容易入手的地方，因为我们已经有一套约 700 个集成测试。然而，有两个问题限制了我们对这些测试的信任，使我们难以用它们来验证如此高风险的迁移是否正确（图 4）。

items.en: **The tests were coupled to the Python implementation.** An integration test sends a request, then checks the reply and what was sent to other services. Our tests ran the Python API inside the test's process and mocked services, like billing and rate limiting, in Python's memory. The tests had to change along with the code, and Claude helped with both. Now, a "pass" could mean that the code was right, or that the test had been changed in a way that let wrong code through. We saw this happen: when we audited the ported tests, we found more than 100 weakened assertions.
items.zh: **测试与 Python 实现耦合。** 一个集成测试会发送请求，然后检查回复以及发送给其他服务的内容。我们的测试在测试进程内运行 Python API，并在 Python 内存中模拟计费、限流等服务。测试必须随代码一起修改，而 Claude 同时协助了这两方面。这样一来，一个“通过”可能意味着代码是正确的，也可能意味着测试被改成了让错误代码通过的形式。我们确实看到了这种情况：在审计移植后的测试时，我们发现了 100 多处被弱化的断言。

items.en: **The tests were incomplete.** The Messages API has dozens of features, and there are far too many configurations to test them exhaustively. Just 20 binary options make over a million combinations—that translates to 12 days of tests at a second each, for one model, before we even vary the prompts inside them. In practice, engineers test a subset that tries to approximate production, but that process inevitably misses cases. Some projects, like Bun, have an independent suite that's extensive enough to judge a rewrite. Many production services don't; what counts as correct depends as much on how they behave as on what's in their tests or documentation.
items.zh: **测试并不完整。** Messages API 有数十项功能，配置组合多到无法穷尽测试。仅 20 个二元选项就能产生超过一百万种组合——对单个模型而言，即使每个测试只花一秒，也需要 12 天，而这还没有考虑其中的提示词变化。在实践中，工程师会测试一个试图近似生产环境的子集，但这一过程不可避免地会遗漏一些情况。有些项目（如 Bun）拥有足够全面的独立测试套件，足以评判一次重写。许多生产服务则没有；所谓“正确”既取决于它们的行为方式，也取决于其测试或文档中的内容。

items.capEn: A ported test may check less than the original (dashed), and tests cover only the combinations someone thought of.
items.capZh: 移植的测试可能比原版检查得更少（虚线），而且测试只覆盖了有人想到的组合。

full.secZh: 在生产环境中检测一致性

items.en: Production data is sometimes “the only true test” that new code behaves like the old code. Running requests through old and new code and comparing the results is often called _shadowing_. To understand what we needed to compare, it helps to walk through what happens to a single request on the Messages API (Figure 5). The API validates each request, converts it into a prompt a model can read (the prompt for inference), tokenizes it, and runs it through safety classifiers. A model then writes a reply, one token at a time. On the output side, the API sorts those tokens into text, thinking, and tool calls, streams them to the customer, and counts usage for limits and billing.
items.zh: 生产数据有时是“唯一真实的测试”，用于验证新代码的行为是否与旧代码一致。将请求分别通过新旧代码运行并比较结果，通常称为**影子测试**。为了理解我们需要比较什么，有必要梳理单个请求在 Messages API 上的处理流程（图 5）。API 会验证每个请求，将其转换为模型可读的提示（用于推理的提示），进行 token 化，并通过安全分类器。然后模型逐个 token 地生成回复。在输出侧，API 将这些 token 分类为文本、思考过程和工具调用，流式传输给客户，并统计用量以用于限制和计费。

items.capEn: The Messages API’s input and output paths. Filled dots are examples of differences we found between Python and Rust. The hollow dot is a risk we had to prevent.
items.capZh: Messages API 的输入和输出路径。实心点是我们在 Python 和 Rust 之间发现的差异示例。空心点是我们必须防范的风险。

items.en: The migration covered both the input and output paths. Some differences were obvious, such as when the Rust API rejected a request that Python had accepted. But many were subtle. For instance, if the Rust API left out part of a prompt, the request would still succeed and the model would still answer, though sometimes with minor differences.
items.zh: 迁移涵盖了输入和输出路径。有些差异很明显，例如 Rust API 拒绝了 Python 原本接受的请求。但许多差异很细微。例如，如果 Rust API 遗漏了提示的一部分，请求仍会成功，模型仍会回答，尽管有时会有细微差别。

items.en: Our Rust API passed about 98% of its tests in April, yet only about a quarter of inputs matched on production traffic (Figure 6). The gap came partly from cases in production traffic that our tests didn’t cover. For example, when Python writes JSON tool calls, it escapes certain characters (e.g., an emoji) by replacing them with text codes. Rust wrote those characters as is, so the two prompts differed by a few bytes. Production also weighted bugs differently. In a test suite, each case counts once, but in live traffic, a bug will show up in each request where it’s triggered, which means a single common bug can cause many mismatches.
items.zh: 我们的 Rust API 在四月份通过了约 98% 的测试，但在生产流量中只有约四分之一的输入匹配（图 6）。差距部分来自生产流量中测试未覆盖的情况。例如，当 Python 写入 JSON 工具调用时，它会通过替换为文本代码来转义某些字符（例如表情符号）。Rust 则原样写入这些字符，因此两个提示相差几个字节。生产环境对缺陷的权重也不同。在测试套件中，每个用例只计一次，但在实时流量中，一个缺陷会在每个触发它的请求中出现，这意味着一个常见的缺陷可能导致许多不匹配。

items.capEn: How often Rust’s input matched Python’s on the requests we compared. Replies were compared separately. Each dot is a day, and the line is a seven-day median. What we compared changed over time, and six misleading days are left out.
items.capZh: 在我们比较的请求上，Rust 的输入与 Python 匹配的频率。回复是单独比较的。每个点代表一天，线是七天中位数。我们比较的内容随时间变化，省略了六个有误导性的日子。

items.en: Common tools for shadowing often assume that a request can safely run twice, or that a service is deterministic. These assumptions didn’t apply in our case. We had to ensure that a request only counted once toward a customer’s limits and bill. In addition, Claude is nondeterministic, meaning that replies can differ for the same input (Figure 7). To address this, we ran the model once and replayed the model output to Rust.
items.zh: 常见的影子测试工具通常假设请求可以安全地运行两次，或者服务是确定性的。这些假设在我们的情况下不适用。我们必须确保一个请求只对客户的限制和账单计数一次。此外，Claude 是非确定性的，意味着相同的输入可能产生不同的回复（图 7）。为了解决这个问题，我们只运行模型一次，并将模型输出重放到 Rust。

items.en: With both versions working from the same model output, we still had to compare every stage before and after the model call, and the results had to match exactly. In many systems, bad input causes an error somewhere down the stack. But since Claude accepts almost any prompt, even a small deviation can change its reply without triggering an error. We compared each step before and after the model call, so that we could pin down any deviation that might change what a customer received.
items.zh: 即使两个版本使用相同的模型输出，我们仍然需要比较模型调用前后的每个阶段，并且结果必须完全匹配。在许多系统中，错误的输入会导致堆栈某处出错。但由于 Claude 几乎接受任何提示，即使很小的偏差也可能改变其回复而不触发错误。我们比较了模型调用前后的每个步骤，以便确定任何可能改变客户所收到内容的偏差。

items.capEn: Diff tools often run the old code twice to learn what varies on its own, then ignore it. Claude's replies vary, so those tools would ignore them, along with any bugs in them.
items.capZh: 差异工具通常会把旧代码运行两次，以了解哪些变化是自身固有的，然后忽略它。Claude 的回复会变化，所以这些工具会忽略它们，连同其中的任何 bug。

items.en: It was important to us to do this in a way that protected user privacy. To do that we had to work without reading user requests or Claude’s replies to them, which means we couldn’t easily see where the Rust and Python versions of the API differed. So instead of looking at text, we recorded the _shape_ of each difference, such as where it happened in the service and how big it was. We did this using a few different approaches:
items.zh: 对我们来说，以保护用户隐私的方式做到这一点很重要。为此，我们必须在无法读取用户请求或 Claude 对其回复的情况下工作，这意味着我们无法轻易看出 Rust 和 Python 版本的 API 在何处存在差异。因此，我们不是查看文本，而是记录每个差异的**形状**，例如它在服务中发生的位置以及它的大小。我们使用了几种不同的方法：

items.en: *   **Checkpointing.** Both API versions handle a request using the same steps: accept or reject it, resolve its settings, build the prompt. Every step produces some result, such as an error or the pieces of the prompt, that we could compare step by step, and within the prompt, piece by piece. The first place they differed indicated roughly where the migration code differed from production code (Figure 8).
items.zh: *   **检查点。** 两个 API 版本使用相同的步骤处理请求：接受或拒绝请求、解析其设置、构建提示。每个步骤都会产生一些结果，例如错误或提示的各个部分，我们可以逐步比较，并在提示内逐片比较。它们首次出现差异的位置大致表明了迁移代码与生产代码的不同之处（图 8）。

items.capEn: Comparing at checkpoints, simplified, with made-up values. The first step to differ shows where to look. The record gives the piece, the lengths, and where they first differ, but not the text.
items.capZh: 在检查点进行比较，简化版，使用虚构的值。第一个出现差异的步骤显示了该从哪里看。记录给出了片段、长度以及它们首次出现差异的位置，但不包含文本。

items.en: *   **Fingerprint.** Once we knew roughly where each diff resided, we still needed a way to distinguish one bug from another. We recorded where each difference began in the prompt, as well as the length difference between the two versions. Combined with the step and piece of the prompt isolated in checkpointing, we found that bugs presented with a specific fingerprint. That is, one bug tends to leave the same fingerprint on every request it affects (Figure 9). We could then group errors by fingerprint, which helped us triage the fixes.
items.zh: *   **指纹。** 一旦我们大致知道每个差异所在的位置，我们仍然需要一种方法来区分一个错误与另一个错误。我们记录了每个差异在提示中开始的位置，以及两个版本之间的长度差异。结合检查点中隔离的步骤和提示片段，我们发现错误呈现出特定的指纹。也就是说，一个错误往往会在它影响的每个请求上留下相同的指纹（图 9）。然后我们可以按指纹对错误进行分组，这有助于我们分类修复。

items.capEn: Fingerprints from one kind of request. A, at the start of the prompt, hid older differences. Once it was fixed, they appeared as B and C. Dots are illustrative.
items.capZh: 来自一种请求的指纹。提示开头的 A 隐藏了较早的差异。一旦修复，它们就作为 B 和 C 出现。点是示意性的。

items.en: The result was a shadowing system that produced a small record of each difference between our Rust and Python APIs. Here is an example, with made-up values:
items.zh: 结果是一个影子系统，它为我们 Rust 和 Python API 之间的每个差异生成一个小记录。以下是一个示例，其中使用了虚构的值：

items.en:
```
step:        build prompt     ← where in the code
piece:       2                ← where in the prompt
first diff:  byte 17          ← fingerprint
python:      190 bytes        ← fingerprint
rust:        190 bytes        ← fingerprint
```
items.zh:
```
step:        build prompt     ← where in the code
piece:       2                ← where in the prompt
first diff:  byte 17          ← fingerprint
python:      190 bytes        ← fingerprint
rust:        190 bytes        ← fingerprint
```

items.en: We could then pass this record to an agent to fix it.
items.zh: 然后我们可以将此记录传递给一个智能体来修复它。

items.en: Each request that differed left a record in our logs. A single bug could produce hundreds of thousands of nearly identical diff records. Rather than send each to an agent, we ran a script every 10 to 30 minutes that grouped them by which fields differed, then alerted a coordinating Claude agent only when it saw a new _kind_ of record. This coordinator assigned a worker agent to own each new kind of record. It also created a new thread in a shared Slack channel where human engineers could follow along and steer it when necessary.
items.zh: 每个出现差异的请求都会在我们的日志中留下一条记录。一个简单的 bug 就可能产生数十万条几乎相同的差异记录。我们没有将每条记录都发送给智能体，而是每 10 到 30 分钟运行一个脚本，按差异字段对记录进行分组，然后仅当发现新**类型**的记录时，才提醒一个协调 Claude 智能体。该协调器会分配一个工作智能体来负责每种新类型的记录。它还会在共享的 Slack 频道中创建一个新线程，以便人类工程师可以跟进并在必要时进行指导。

items.en: To tackle the many bugs, we set up a series of verification loops. A fast _inner_ loop gave agents a sandbox in which they could test ideas and propose fixes. A slower _outer_ loop then validated fixes in production. In addition, a _memory loop_ recorded any mistakes along the way, saving them so that agents could learn over time (Figure 10).
items.zh: 为了解决众多 bug，我们建立了一系列验证循环。一个快速的**内层**循环为智能体提供了一个沙盒，在其中可以测试想法并提出修复方案。一个较慢的**外层**循环则验证生产环境中的修复。此外，一个**记忆循环**记录过程中的任何错误，将其保存下来，以便智能体可以随时间学习（图 10）。

items.capEn: Verification loops. An edit is checked in a sandbox, and then on shadowed live traffic. People’s corrections become rules. Each loop can catch what the one inside it misses.
items.capZh: 验证循环。编辑先在沙箱中检查，然后在影子实时流量上检查。人们的修正会成为规则。每个循环都能捕捉到内层循环遗漏的东西。

items.en: When we first started testing this in April, we gave each agent a record that showed where the Rust and Python versions differed. Agents would guess the root cause from the code and open a pull request. Once the fix was reviewed and merged, they deployed it to staging, a preproduction copy of the Rust API where we ran the same shadow comparison on test traffic. The agents checked whether the difference was eliminated. Since every hypothesis needed a review and a deployment, feedback was taking hours or days.
items.zh: 我们在四月首次开始测试时，给每个智能体一条记录，显示 Rust 与 Python 版本在何处存在差异。智能体会根据代码猜测根本原因，并提交一个 pull request。修复经过评审并合并后，他们将其部署到 staging——Rust API 的一个预发布副本，我们在测试流量上运行同样的影子对比。智能体检查差异是否被消除。由于每个假设都需要一次评审和一次部署，反馈要花上数小时甚至数天。

items.en: We needed agents to get a signal from verification much sooner, so we moved them into their own workspace. We redesigned the inner loop so that agents could have a place to test ideas quickly and fail safely. Each agent ran in a cloud sandbox with both codebases and fast, local checks for what happens before and after the model call. The input check took a request, built the prompt that each version would send to the model, and showed what differed. Because this check never actually called the model, comparing the versions took under a second. We later added an output check, which ran both versions against a fake model. The output check passed a scripted reply, such as a tool call, through each version and compared the results.
items.zh: 我们需要智能体更快地从验证中获得信号，于是把它们移入各自的工作区。我们重新设计了内循环，使智能体有一个可以快速试验想法并安全失败的地方。每个智能体都在一个云沙箱中运行，其中包含两个代码库，以及针对模型调用前后所发生情况的快速本地检查。输入检查接收一个请求，构建每个版本将发送给模型的 prompt，并显示差异所在。由于该检查从不真正调用模型，比较两个版本耗时不到一秒。我们后来增加了输出检查，让两个版本针对一个假模型运行。输出检查将一段脚本化的回复（例如一次工具调用）分别通过每个版本，并比较结果。

items.en: The main limitation was that agents could only see the fingerprint, not the request behind each record. So an agent would hypothesize what had caused the difference, then write its own request or model reply to try to reproduce the difference. Since each agent was writing these itself, it could read both results in full. If the results matched, its guess was wrong and the agent tried again. If they differed the same way the record described, the agent edited the Rust until the two versions matched, then added a test that failed on the old code and passed on the new (Figure 11).
items.zh: 主要限制在于智能体只能看到指纹，而看不到每条记录背后的请求。因此智能体会假设差异的成因，然后自己编写请求或模型回复，试图复现该差异。由于这些内容由每个智能体自行编写，它可以完整读取两个结果。如果结果相同，说明它的猜测有误，智能体会再试一次。如果它们以记录所描述的相同方式出现差异，智能体就修改 Rust，直到两个版本一致，然后添加一个在旧代码上失败、在新代码上通过的测试（图 11）。

items.capEn: Inner loop. From a fingerprint, an agent guesses the cause and writes a request or reply that should trigger it. Local checks run it through both versions until an edit makes them match.
items.capZh: 内循环。智能体根据指纹猜测原因，并编写应能触发该原因的请求或回复。本地检查会让两个版本都运行它，直到某次编辑使二者匹配。

items.en: The seam between the inner and outer loops was a good checkpoint for human review. Inside the sandbox, a wrong guess cost an agent only a few seconds and had no impact on users. Agents could iterate on their own. We allowed a fix to cross into the outer loop only after it had undergone PR review; this allowed engineers to focus their attention on proposed fixes (rather than on guesses) and on the questions the verifiers couldn't answer, such as whether a difference between the Rust and Python APIs was the result of a bug or a deliberate change.
items.zh: 内循环与外循环之间的接缝是人类评审的良好检查点。在沙箱内，一次错误猜测只让智能体花费几秒钟，且对用户没有影响。智能体可以自行迭代。只有当修复经过 PR 评审后，我们才允许它进入外循环；这使工程师能够将注意力集中在所提议的修复上（而非猜测上），以及验证器无法回答的问题上，例如 Rust 与 Python API 之间的差异是 bug 导致的，还是有意为之的变更。

items.en: Agents posted their fixes and evidence to their Slack threads for engineers to review. In mid-May, one of the largest remaining differences between the Rust and Python APIs came from web search. The production API retrieved the web search tool's description from an internal service. The Rust API didn't call this service yet, so the tool description was missing from the prompts. An agent proposed a shortcut to copy the text into files that would be readable by Rust. The prompts then matched, and the fix passed the local verifier. But an engineer turned it down because it didn't solve the problem: Rust would still need to call the service before launch, at which point the workaround would be thrown out (Figure 12).
items.zh: 智能体将修复和证据发布到各自的 Slack 线程中供工程师评审。五月中旬，Rust 与 Python API 之间剩余的最大差异之一来自网络搜索。生产 API 从内部服务获取网络搜索工具的描述。Rust API 尚未调用该服务，因此 prompt 中缺少工具描述。一个智能体提出了一种捷径：将文本复制到 Rust 可读取的文件中。于是 prompt 匹配了，修复也通过了本地验证器。但一位工程师否决了它，因为它没有解决问题：Rust 在发布前仍需要调用该服务，到那时这个变通方案就会被丢弃（图 12）。

items.en: But the verifier rewarded matching outputs, and the agent found the cheapest way to produce them. A verifier can tell an agent whether the outputs matched, but not whether the fix is good enough to ship. That's why human review was an important gate.
items.zh: 但验证器奖励的是输出匹配，而智能体找到了产生这些匹配输出的最廉价方式。验证器可以告诉智能体输出是否匹配，却无法判断修复是否好到足以发布。正因如此，人工审查才是一道重要的关卡。

items.capEn: Agents trace a mismatch to the web search tool across four Slack threads and propose a fix, which an engineer rejects as throwaway code. We shortened and reworded the messages and added the thread names and agent labels.
items.capZh: 智能体在四个 Slack 线程中把一处不匹配追溯到网页搜索工具，并提出修复方案，但被工程师以一次性代码为由拒绝。我们缩短并改写了消息，还添加了线程名称和智能体标签。

items.en: In the inner loop, agents debugged differences and proposed fixes. At the seam between the inner loop and the outer loop, engineers reviewed the proposed fixes, gave feedback, and approved them to deploy. The outer loop then compared Rust API deployments with and without each fix.
items.zh: 在内循环中，智能体对差异进行调试并提出修复方案。在内循环与外循环的衔接处，工程师审查所提出的修复方案、给出反馈，并批准其部署。随后，外循环对应用了各项修复与未应用修复的 Rust API 部署进行比较。

items.en: To make that comparison fair, we logged facts about each request we compared, but not its text, including which model and API features it used—for example, prompt caching, tools, or extended thinking. These details let agents compare requests of the same kind (Figure 13) and ask how often the bug's fingerprint appeared on builds with and without the fix. This way, agents could monitor the new builds for the bug.
items.zh: 为使比较公平，我们记录了所比较的每个请求的相关事实（但不记录其文本），包括该请求使用了哪个模型以及哪些 API 功能——例如提示缓存、工具或扩展思考。这些细节使智能体能够比较同类请求（图 13），并考察该 bug 的指纹在应用修复与未应用修复的构建上出现的频率。通过这种方式，智能体可以在新构建上监控该 bug。

items.capEn: Outer loop. An engineer reviews the fix, it deploys, and shadowed traffic shows whether its fingerprint is gone. If not, the task returns to the inner loop.
items.capZh: 外循环。工程师审查修复方案，随后部署，影子流量显示其指纹是否消失。若未消失，任务则返回内循环。

items.en: We designed the outer loop to catch problems that the inner loop missed. The inner loop simulated production quickly but imperfectly: agents could test a hypothesis in seconds, but only on requests they had written, and with a local verifier that wasn't always configured exactly like production.
items.zh: 我们设计外循环，是为了捕捉内循环遗漏的问题。内循环对生产环境的模拟快速但不完美：智能体可以在数秒内检验一个假设，但只能针对自己编写的请求，且所使用的本地验证器并不总是与生产环境完全一致地配置。

items.en: This means that sometimes a fix passed in the sandbox and production still showed the difference. The agent assigned to the bug would either see the difference in the new build's records, or be alerted by the coordinating agent. It then went back to the inner loop and used that evidence to form a new hypothesis.
items.zh: 这意味着，有时某个修复在沙箱中通过了，但生产环境仍然显示出差异。负责该 bug 的智能体会在新构建的记录中看到该差异，或被协调智能体提醒。随后它回到内循环，利用该证据形成新的假设。

items.en: The inner and outer loops fixed one difference at a time. The memory loop improved how agents made those fixes. We didn’t want engineers to have to make the same correction twice, so we recorded what came out of reviews and agents’ own work and applied it to every agent that followed.
items.zh: 内循环和外循环每次只修复一个差异。记忆循环改进了智能体进行这些修复的方式。我们不希望工程师不得不重复同样的修正，因此我们记录了评审和智能体自身工作的结果，并将其应用于后续的每个智能体。

items.en: For example, when an engineer turned down the web search shortcut (Figure 12), the agent saved a note to memory explaining the decision, the reason for it, and the correct fix, which was to have Rust call the service that supplies tool descriptions.
items.zh: 例如，当一位工程师拒绝了网络搜索的捷径（图 12）时，智能体将一条笔记保存到记忆中，解释了该决定、其原因以及正确的修复方法，即让 Rust 调用提供工具描述的服务。

items.en: Building that call took our team weeks, and in the meantime the bug kept producing records. Some had new fingerprints, because the missing text fell at other positions in the prompt or belonged to another tool that used the same service. Agents checked the memory note, recognized the known bug, and linked those records to it, instead of writing another workaround (Figure 14).
items.zh: 构建该调用花了我们团队数周时间，在此期间，该缺陷不断产生记录。有些记录具有新的指纹，因为缺失的文本出现在提示中的其他位置，或者属于使用同一服务的另一个工具。智能体检查了记忆笔记，识别出已知缺陷，并将这些记录链接到它，而不是编写另一个变通方法（图 14）。

items.en: Other lessons became general rules for porting and writing Rust. After one agent guessed at Python’s behavior, an engineer made it a rule to port exactly what Python did. An agent then compared the existing code with that rule and found seven more places where the port had relied on a guess.
items.zh: 其他经验成为了移植和编写 Rust 的通用规则。在一个智能体对 Python 的行为进行了猜测之后，一位工程师制定了一条规则：精确移植 Python 的行为。然后，一个智能体将现有代码与该规则进行比较，又发现了七处移植依赖猜测的地方。

items.en: In June, an agent also went through about 60 of the team’s review comments, grouped the recurring problems and proposed rules, which an engineer edited and approved for CLAUDE.md (Figure 14).
items.zh: 六月份，一个智能体还梳理了团队约 60 条评审意见，将反复出现的问题分组并提出规则，由一位工程师编辑并批准写入 CLAUDE.md（图 14）。

items.en: The memory loop also encoded some lessons in permanent checks. This included new tests that failed when Rust drifted from Python, lints that banned patterns reviewers kept flagging, and later a merge check that required anyone changing the Python code to make a matching change in Rust or request an exemption.
items.zh: 记忆循环还将一些经验固化为永久性检查。这包括：当 Rust 与 Python 出现偏差时就会失败的新测试、禁止审查者反复标记的模式的 lint 规则，以及后来的一项合并检查——要求任何修改 Python 代码的人都必须在 Rust 中做出相应修改，或申请豁免。

items.capEn: Memory loop. An engineer’s correction becomes three things: a rule that each new agent reads, a search for the same mistake, and a test.
items.capZh: 记忆循环。工程师的纠正会转化为三样东西：每个新智能体都会读取的规则、对同一错误的搜索，以及一项测试。

paras.en: It's increasingly feasible to migrate production systems with Claude, either for better performance or security, without taking an API offline or slowing feature development. Now that the hard part is no longer writing new code, we need to build sufficient confidence that the new system behaves like the old one.
paras.zh: 使用 Claude 迁移生产系统正变得越来越可行，无论是为了更好的性能还是安全性，都无需让 API 下线或减慢功能开发。既然困难的部分不再是编写新代码，我们需要建立足够的信心，确保新系统的行为与旧系统一致。

paras.en: The usual approach to migration is a bit like rebuilding the Ship of Theseus, in which the old ship was replaced plank by plank. Generally it's been possible to replace planks while the ship still sails, but changing too many planks at once requires coming into dock. To fully stretch the metaphor, Claude now makes it possible to build an identically functioning ship alongside the first—even as the first keeps sailing and having its planks replaced. Agents kept the new ship in step as the old one changed, and we kept checking that the two behaved the same. Once we trusted that they did, we moved the passengers over a few at a time. The new ship sails faster and more efficiently than the old one.
paras.zh: 通常的迁移方法有点像重建忒修斯之船，即一块一块地更换旧船的木板。一般来说，可以在船仍在航行时更换木板，但一次更换太多木板就需要进港。充分延伸这个比喻，Claude 现在使得可以 alongside 第一艘船建造一艘功能相同的船——即使第一艘船继续航行并更换木板。智能体让新船与旧船的变化保持同步，我们不断检查两者行为是否相同。一旦我们相信它们确实如此，我们就一次几个地把乘客转移过去。新船比旧船航行得更快、更高效。

items.en: **Verification is the new bottleneck.** Previously, large software projects like migrations were hard to justify because they took too much effort and carried too much risk. But if writing code is no longer the bottleneck, the main constraint becomes how quickly you can verify results. In general, ambition can be increased as long as there’s a way for Claude to verify correctness.
items.zh: **验证是新的瓶颈。** 以前，像迁移这样的大型软件项目很难被证明合理，因为它们需要太多精力并承担太多风险。但如果编写代码不再是瓶颈，主要限制就变成了你能多快地验证结果。一般来说，只要有一种方法让 Claude 验证正确性，就可以提高雄心。

items.en: **Verification is how you earn confidence.** In math, we use a proof assistant to verify that each step of a proof Claude wrote is valid. For software, tests or formal verification can help us gain similar confidence. But when these checks aren’t enough, a production system itself can also be a verifier.
items.zh: **验证是你获得信心的方式。** 在数学中，我们使用证明助手来验证 Claude 所写证明的每一步是否有效。对于软件，测试或形式化验证可以帮助我们获得类似的信心。但当这些检查不够时，生产系统本身也可以作为验证器。

items.en: **Carefully design the verification signal.** A verifier provides a signal that Claude can act on. We can calibrate this signal to show Claude where things went wrong. Where a proof assistant points to the failing step or a test names the failing case, a production system often offers no such signal by default. Much of our effort for this project went to building such a signal. In this case, checkpoints located each difference _in the code_ and fingerprints helped _tell one bug from another_.
items.zh: **仔细设计验证信号。** 验证器提供了一种 Claude 可以据此行动的信号。我们可以校准这个信号，以向 Claude 显示哪里出了问题。证明助手会指出失败的步骤，测试会指出失败的案例，而生产系统通常默认不提供这样的信号。我们在这个项目上的大部分努力都用于构建这样的信号。在这种情况下，检查点定位了 _代码中_ 的每个差异，而指纹有助于 _区分一个错误和另一个错误_。

items.en: **Build loops that let Claude autonomously act on the signal.** Our inner loop was fast and ran locally in a sandbox. Agents tested hypotheses in seconds using requests they wrote themselves. The outer loop was slower and checked fixes on shadowed production traffic. The outermost loop was just prose, with corrections saved as rules in memory that could be read by every agent later in the process. Together, these loops allowed us to migrate the Messages API to Rust, which uses about 70% less CPU per request and reduces median time to first token by about 20% (Figure 15).
items.zh: **构建让 Claude 自主根据信号行动的循环。** 我们的内循环很快，并在沙箱中本地运行。智能体使用自己编写的请求在几秒钟内测试假设。外循环较慢，并在影子生产流量上检查修复。最外层循环只是文字说明，将修正保存为记忆中的规则，供流程中后续的每个智能体读取。这些循环共同使我们能够将 Messages API 迁移到 Rust，每个请求使用的 CPU 减少约 70%，并将首个 token 的中位时间减少了约 20%（图 15）。

items.capEn: CPU and memory used per request, and median time to first token, as requests moved from Python (gray) to Rust (blue). Lines are seven-day averages, 100 is about the level just before the move, and each arrow shows the change from the first dot to the second. CPU is one region, memory is all of production, and time to first token is customers' Claude Code requests over a shorter period. In the third panel, the fall before the first dot came while almost all of those requests were still on Python.
items.capZh: 随着请求从 Python（灰色）迁移到 Rust（蓝色），每请求的 CPU 和内存用量，以及首 token 中位时间。折线为七日平均值，100 约为迁移前水平，每个箭头表示从第一个点到第二个点的变化。CPU 为一个区域，内存为全部生产环境，首 token 时间为客户 Claude Code 请求在较短时期内的数据。在第三幅图中，第一个点之前的下降发生在几乎所有此类请求仍运行于 Python 时。

items.en: **Keep the loops simple, so they scale with Claude’s capability.** We tried to put human judgment only into what counted as correct; otherwise we left it up to Claude how to get there. Agents chose which hypotheses to test, how to reproduce each bug, and how to fix it. The verifiers judged the result. Simple loops around strong verifiers allowed us to move productively over time (Figure 16).
items.zh: **保持循环简单，以便它们随 Claude 的能力扩展。** 我们试图只将人类判断放在什么算作正确上；否则，我们让 Claude 自行决定如何达到目标。智能体选择测试哪些假设、如何复现每个错误以及如何修复它。验证器判断结果。围绕强大验证器的简单循环使我们能够随着时间的推移高效推进（图 16）。

items.capEn: Changes merged to our API's Rust code in each two-week period, from April until public traffic moved to Rust in September 2026. Not all of them are migration work.
items.capZh: 从四月到 2026 年九月公共流量迁移至 Rust 期间，每两周合并到我们 API 的 Rust 代码中的变更。并非所有变更都属于迁移工作。

items.en: **Move toward outer loops.** At first, we had our engineers working inside the inner loop, running Claude and chasing differences themselves. Later, they moved to the seam between loops, helping to steer agents and reviewing fixes in Slack. But as the system matured, they increasingly moved to the edge, where they could provide the highest leverage, writing the rules and checks that agents worked within. As Claude grew more intelligent (and as we grew more intelligent at working with it), we evolved from directing Claude to Claude directing itself, relying on humans mainly for important judgment calls.
items.zh: **向外层循环迁移。** 起初，我们让工程师在内层循环中工作，亲自运行 Claude 并追查差异。后来，他们转移到循环之间的接缝处，帮助引导智能体并在 Slack 中审查修复。但随着系统逐渐成熟，他们越来越多地转向边缘位置，在那里能发挥最大的杠杆作用——编写智能体工作所遵循的规则与检查。随着 Claude 变得更智能（我们也变得更善于与它协作），我们从“指挥 Claude”演进为“Claude 指挥自身”，人类主要负责重要的判断决策。
